readerQuestion: How can I temporarily change my lights in Home Assistant and then restore each light to the state it had beforehand?
directAnswer: Capture each individual light with scene.create before changing it, then call scene.turn_on from the same single-mode script after the short delay. This preserves mixed starting on/off states without a second call overwriting the capture. Temporary scenes disappear on restart or scene reload, and an off lamp’s next-on brightness is not guaranteed. Start with the 30-second two-lamp check before extending the duration.
originalContribution: The #setup configuration supplies a complete two-lamp script with an on/off-state guard, one active run, a reserved snapshot name and cleanup. The #worked-example table follows one lamp at about 30% and another initially off through an 80% boost, repeat call and restoration. It adds the separate next-on-brightness check that a simple save/restore recipe misses. #troubleshooting distinguishes group capture, overwrite, off-state memory, interruption and partial device response.

claimChecks.claim: scene.create accepts snapshot_entities, creates a temporary scene and overwrites an existing dynamically created scene with the same ID; restart or scene reload removes it.
scene.turn_on activates the saved states; scene.delete removes dynamically created scenes rather than turning lamps off.
Script single mode rejects another run while one is active; restart stops the previous run, queued defers subsequent runs and parallel permits simultaneous runs.
A condition in the main script sequence stops execution when false; a delay suspends the sequence before later actions.
A standard light group reports on when at least one member is on; recording that aggregate does not encode each member’s separate on/off choice.
For captured off states, current light restoration code calls turn_off without programming next-on brightness; for captured on states it uses saved supported brightness and color attributes.
The snapshot implementation copies each named entity’s current state and attributes from Home Assistant rather than requesting fresh hardware readings.
